title: NDA 2026 - Join Army, Navy & Air Force After Class 12
meta_description: NDA 2 2026: 394 vacancies (370 male, 24 female) for Army, Navy, Air Force wings. Exam 13 Sep 2026. Apply 20 May-9 Jun. Age 16.5-19.5. Class 12 PCM required.

hero.one_liner: Gateway to Indian Armed Forces as an officer - join Army, Navy, or Air Force through India's premier defence training academy after 12th

what_is_it: The National Defence Academy (NDA) exam is conducted by UPSC twice a year (NDA I and NDA II) to recruit candidates for the NDA and Naval Academy courses. NDA is the premier tri-service training academy located in Khadakwasla, Pune, where cadets are trained for 3 years before being commissioned as officers in the Indian Army, Navy, or Air Force.

The exam is open to 12th pass or appearing candidates aged 16.5-19.5 years. For Army wing, any stream (Arts/Science/Commerce) works. For Navy and Air Force, 12th with Physics and Mathematics is mandatory. After clearing the written exam (conducted by UPSC), candidates appear for SSB Interview (5-day assessment) which tests personality, officer-like qualities, and leadership potential.

NDA is considered one of the most prestigious career paths for young Indians. Officers commissioned through NDA are highly respected and receive excellent training, salary, and perks. Starting salary after training is approximately ₹56,100 basic + allowances = ₹70,000-90,000/month, with free accommodation, medical, canteen, and other facilities.
NDA I 2026 exam is scheduled for 13 April 2026. The notification is typically released 3-4 months before the exam date.

extra_sections.heading: NDA - the fastest path to officer rank
content: NDA (National Defence Academy) is India's premier tri-service training academy in Khadakwasla, Pune. Cadets join after 12th class (age 16.5-19.5) and undergo 3 years of training + 1 year at their respective service academy (IMA/INA/AFA).

Upon graduation, they're commissioned as Lieutenant with immediate officer status. NDA is the fastest and youngest entry into officer rank - you become a Lieutenant at age 22-23, while CDS (Combined Defence Services) graduates become officers at 25-26 and AFCAT officers at 24-25.

The early start compounds over your career - NDA officers typically retire at higher ranks than later-entry officers. The training is holistic - academic degree (BA/BSc/BCom from Jawaharlal Nehru University), physical training, military training, adventure activities, and character building.
NDA graduates form the backbone of India's military leadership - the bond and network formed here lasts a lifetime.

extra_sections.heading: NDA eligibility - age, stream and who can apply
content: You must be unmarried to apply, and you must stay unmarried through the entire training period. Marrying during training means discharge and refunding the training cost.
The age window is narrow: 16.5 to 19.5 years on the date fixed in the notification. UPSC specifies an exact band of birth dates each cycle, so check it carefully.
For the Army wing, any Class 12 pass qualifies whatever your stream. For the Air Force, Navy and Naval Academy wings, you must have studied Physics and Maths in Class 12.
Both unmarried male and female candidates can now apply across all wings. Women have been eligible since 2022, and NDA II 2026 set aside 24 of its 394 seats for them.
You must be a citizen of India, or fall within the specific categories UPSC lists. Candidates appearing in Class 12 can apply, provided they prove passing by the course deadline.
There is no cap on attempts as long as you stay inside the age window. Because that window is so tight, most aspirants realistically get only two or three genuine shots at the exam.

extra_sections.heading: NDA written exam - detailed section strategy
content: Mathematics (300 marks): This paper covers Class 11-12 level math - Algebra (quadratic equations, complex numbers, permutation-combination, binomial theorem), Matrices and Determinants, Trigonometry (identities, inverse functions, height and distance), Analytical Geometry (2D and 3D), Differential Calculus (limits, continuity, differentiation, maxima-minima), Integral Calculus (integration methods, definite integrals, area under curves), Vector Algebra, and Statistics and Probability. The math paper is what separates NDA from other defense exams.

If you're strong in Class 11-12 math, you have a significant advantage. Arts stream students often struggle here - if math is your weakness, start preparation from Class 11 NCERT and build up gradually.
RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics and Pathfinder NDA by Arihant are the standard books. Focus on Trigonometry and Calculus - they carry approximately 100 marks combined (33% of the paper).
Master the 20 most common trigonometric identities and the 10 standard integration formulas. These formulas appear in some form in every single NDA paper.
Create a formula sheet and revise it daily for the last 2 months. GAT - General Ability Test (600 marks): Divided into English (200 marks) and General Knowledge (400 marks).
English tests comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, and usage through MCQs. GK covers Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Indian History, Geography, Current Affairs, and General Science.

extra_sections.heading: NDA Scoring Strategy & Cutoff
content: NDA written exam has 2 papers: Mathematics (300 marks, 120 questions) and GAT (600 marks, 150 questions). Total: 900 marks.
SSB Interview adds 900 marks, making the final merit out of 1800. Written exam cutoff for General category typically ranges from 340-370 marks (out of 900).
This means you need approximately 38-41% to clear the written stage. However, the SSB interview rejection rate is 85-90%, so clearing the written exam is just the beginning.
The safest strategy: aim for 180+ in Mathematics and 200+ in GAT. Mathematics is the differentiator - most candidates score similarly in GAT, but strong math performance creates a comfortable buffer.
Focus on Calculus, Matrices, and Trigonometry which together carry 100+ marks.

steps.title: Day 1: Screening
steps.desc: Officer Intelligence Rating plus Picture Perception and Discussion. Many candidates are screened out on day one.

steps.title: Day 2: Psychology tests
steps.desc: TAT, WAT, SRT and Self-Description. These probe your personality through quick written responses under time pressure.

steps.title: Days 3-4: Group tasks (GTO)
steps.desc: Group discussion, group tasks, lecturette and the command task. The GTO watches how you think and lead in a team.

steps.title: Day 4-5: Interview & conference
steps.desc: A personal interview and the final board conference that decides your recommendation. A medical follows for recommended candidates.

extra_sections.heading: SSB interview - the real filter
extra_sections.content:
The written exam shortlists 5-6x the vacancies. SSB (Services Selection Board) interview is the real selection - only 10-15% clear it.

The 5-day assessment tests OLQs (Officer Like Qualities): initiative, determination, courage, group planning, and communication. You can't fake it - SSB tests your natural personality.

Start group discussions, sports, and leadership activities NOW to develop these traits naturally.

items.title: Officer from day one
items.sub: You are commissioned as a Lieutenant or equivalent, leading soldiers in your early twenties with real responsibility.

items.title: Pay and perks
items.sub: Gross pay around ₹80,000 to ₹1.2 lakh, plus free accommodation, family medical care, canteen and travel concessions.

items.title: Postings and variety
items.sub: Postings span peace and field areas, from cities to high-altitude borders, with allowances that rise with the toughness of the posting.

items.title: Growth and respect
items.sub: A structured promotion ladder, lifelong pension, and a level of respect and adventure few civilian jobs match. Officers also retire earlier than most government staff, with full pension benefits.

extra_sections.heading: NDA training - 3 years at the academy
content: NDA (Khadakwasla, Pune) training spans 6 semesters over 3 years. Cadets pursue a BA/BSc/BCom degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University simultaneously with military training.

The academic curriculum includes subjects relevant to your chosen service - Army cadets study military history and strategy, Navy cadets study navigation and marine engineering, Air Force cadets study aerodynamics and aviation. Physical training is intense and progressive: morning PT at 5:30 AM (running, swimming, cross-country, assault course), followed by drill, weapon training, map reading, field craft, and tactical exercises.
Swimming is mandatory - you must pass a swimming test in the first term. Non-swimmers receive compulsory swimming coaching.

The famous NDA traditions: inter-squadron competitions in sports, debates, and cultural events build camaraderie and competitive spirit. The passing out parade at the end of 3 years is attended by the President or Defense Minister.

NDA friendships last a lifetime - the bond formed through shared physical and mental challenges during training is unlike anything in civilian life. After NDA: Army cadets go to Indian Military Academy (IMA, Dehradun) for 1 year.
Navy cadets go to Indian Naval Academy (INA, Ezhimala) for 1 year. Air Force cadets go to Air Force Academy (AFA, Dundigal) for 1.5 years.

Upon successful completion, you're commissioned as a Lieutenant (Army), Sub-Lieutenant (Navy), or Flying Officer (Air Force) with full officer status and permanent commission. For more details, see our guide on SSC GD Constable 2026.

items.title: 3 years at NDA, Khadakwasla
items.sub: Joint training for Army, Navy and Air Force cadets, with a JNU degree (BA, BSc or BTech) alongside military training.

items.title: 1 year at your service academy
items.sub: Army cadets go to IMA Dehradun, Navy to INA Ezhimala, and Air Force to AFA Hyderabad for pre-commission training.

items.title: Commission as an officer
items.sub: You pass out as a Lieutenant, Sub-Lieutenant or Flying Officer and begin your service career.

extra_sections.title: Final merit is out of 1800
extra_sections.desc: The written exam carries 900 marks and the SSB another 900. Since the two weigh equally, a strong SSB performance matters just as much as your written score.

extra_sections.heading: NDA vs CDS vs Agnipath - Which Path to Choose?
NDA preparation - 6 month plan for Class 11-12 students
content: Month 1-2 (Math foundation): Complete Class 11 math from NCERT - Algebra, Trigonometry, Coordinate Geometry, Statistics. Solve RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics chapter-wise.
Simultaneously start reading newspaper daily for GK and English improvement. Begin light physical training - running 2km, pushups, pullups.
Month 3-4 (GK + English depth): Complete Class 12 math (Calculus, Vectors, Probability). Start GK preparation - NCERT History Class 6-12, Geography Class 6-12, Science Class 9-10.
Practice English grammar from Wren & Martin. Increase physical training - 5km runs, swimming practice, obstacle course at local army coaching.
Month 5 (Mock tests): Take 2 full-length NDA mocks per week. Analyze math paper mistakes - identify topics where you consistently lose marks.
Revise GK notes weekly. Practice English comprehension passages daily.
Physical fitness should be at SSB standard - 2.4km run under 12 minutes, 10+ pullups, 30+ pushups. Month 6 (Final revision): Take 1 mock daily in the last 2 weeks.
Revise math formula sheet every morning. Revise 6-month current affairs compilation.

Practice PPDT (Picture Perception and Description Test) with friends - this is the Day 1 screening test at SSB. Sleep well, eat well, and maintain your physical fitness - SSB is physically and mentally demanding.

extra_sections.heading: Physical fitness requirements and preparation
content: SSB physical standards: Height - minimum 157cm for Army, 157cm for Navy, 162.5cm for Air Force (male). For female candidates: 152cm minimum.
Weight proportional to height (BMI 18-25). Vision: 6/6 in better eye, 6/9 in worse eye without glasses for Army.

Air Force flying branch requires 6/6 in both eyes without glasses - LASIK is accepted if done 6 months prior. Individual obstacles at SSB: You face 10 obstacles - rope climbing (6 meters), balance beam, Burma bridge, tiger leap (jumping across a gap), commando walk (rope traverse), and others.
Each obstacle tests a different physical skill - upper body strength, balance, agility, and courage. Practice at your local Army coaching center or gymnasium.
Physical preparation timeline: Start 6 months before the expected SSB date. Month 1-2: Build basic fitness - daily running (3km), 20 pushups, 5 pullups, 30 squats.

Month 3-4: Increase intensity - 5km runs under 25 minutes, 40 pushups, 10 pullups, obstacle practice. Month 5-6: Peak fitness - run 2.4km in under 10 minutes, 50 pushups, 15 pullups, all individual obstacles comfortable.
Swimming is mandatory: NDA training includes compulsory swimming. If you can't swim, learn now - join a local swimming class.
You need to swim 100 meters without stopping. At NDA, non-swimmers receive intensive coaching, but having basic swimming skills before joining reduces stress during the first term significantly.

extra_sections.heading: NDA medical standards - what gets people rejected

items.title: Eyesight
items.sub: Vision norms are strict, and stricter for flying and naval branches. Colour blindness rules out the flying branch entirely, so know your status early.

items.title: Height & weight
items.sub: There is a minimum height with weight matched to height and age. Being underweight or overweight at the medical can cost you a recommendation.

items.title: Common rejections
items.sub: Flat feet, knock knees, poor eyesight and certain old injuries are frequent reasons. A basic check early lets you fix correctable issues, and minor ones like dental problems can often be treated before the medical board.

items.title: Tattoos & other rules
items.sub: Tattoos in non-permitted areas can disqualify you. Read the medical guidelines in the notification before you set your heart on a particular wing.

extra_sections.heading: Books and coaching for NDA
content: Standard books: Pathfinder NDA/NA by Arihant (comprehensive - covers math, English, and GK in one book), RS Aggarwal NDA Mathematics (best for math practice), Lucent's General Knowledge (covers all GK topics), Wren and Martin English Grammar. These 4 books are sufficient for 95% of NDA preparation.
Don't buy more than 4-5 books - depth in fewer books beats surface-level coverage across many. Free resources: NDA previous year papers with solutions are available on UPSC website (upsc.gov.in).
NCERT textbooks (free PDFs at ncert.nic.in) cover 70% of the GK syllabus. YouTube channels like Defence Guru, MKC, and SSBCrack offer free NDA preparation lectures and SSB guidance.

Coaching institutes: Centurion Defence Academy (Lucknow), Major Kalshi Classes (Allahabad), Shield Defence Academy (Delhi) are popular for NDA coaching. Fees range from Rs 30,000-80,000 for 6-12 month programs.

Online coaching (Unacademy NDA, Testbook Defence) costs Rs 5,000-15,000 and covers the same syllabus. Self-study works well for NDA if you're disciplined with NCERT textbooks and previous year papers.

extra_sections.heading: NDA salary and benefits
extra_sections.content:
During training, cadets get a fixed stipend of ₹56,100 a month. On commissioning as a Lieutenant, basic pay is ₹56,100 plus ₹15,500 Military Service Pay, taking gross to roughly ₹80,000 to ₹1,20,000 with DA and allowances.

Officers also get free accommodation, family medical care, canteen access and pension benefits.

extra_sections.text: NDA is the youngest entry into the Indian Armed Forces - cadets who clear it at 16-17 years of age retire as senior officers with a lifetime of service, honour, and one of the best pension packages in the country.

preparation_tips: Mathematics paper (300 marks) is the game-changer. If you're weak in Math, NDA will be very tough. Cover: Algebra, Matrices, Trigonometry, Calculus (basics), Analytical Geometry, Vector Algebra, Statistics, and Probability. Use NCERT 11th-12th Math textbooks as primary resource.

General Ability Test Paper 2 has two sections: English (200 marks) and General Knowledge (400 marks). GK covers Physics, Chemistry, Biology, History, Geography, Current Affairs, and Defence-related topics. Focus on NCERT 6-12 for science and social studies.

Start SSB preparation from Day 1 - don't wait till after the written exam. Read newspapers daily, develop opinions on national/international issues, practice group discussions with friends, and work on your physical fitness. SSB evaluates your personality over 5 days - it can't be faked.

Physical fitness is essential - not for the written exam but for SSB (obstacle course, outdoor tasks) and the 3-year NDA training which is very physically demanding. Start running, swimming, and body-weight exercises now. Target: 5 km run in under 25 minutes.

faqs.question: Can girls apply for NDA?
faqs.answer:
Yes. The Supreme Court ordered women's admission to NDA in 2021, and female candidates have been appearing since 2022.

Women can join the Army and Air Force wings through NDA. The training and curriculum are the same.

Women officers are fully commissioned with equal ranks and pay.

faqs.question: What degree do you get at NDA?
faqs.answer:
NDA cadets earn a Bachelor's degree from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) during their 3-year training. Army cadets get BA/BSc.

Navy and Air Force cadets get BSc. The degree is fully recognized and equivalent to any regular university degree.

faqs.question: What if I clear the written exam but fail SSB?
faqs.answer:
You can appear again in the next NDA exam cycle (NDA I or NDA II) as long as you meet the age criteria. Many successful NDA candidates clear SSB on their 2nd or 3rd attempt.

Each SSB attempt teaches you something and improves your chances. Retain your written exam result for analysis - understand what went wrong in SSB.

faqs.question: NDA salary after training?
faqs.answer:
During the 3-year training, cadets get a fixed stipend of ₹56,100 a month. After commissioning as a Lieutenant, basic pay is ₹56,100 at Pay Level 10.

With Military Service Pay of ₹15,500 plus DA and allowances, gross reaches roughly ₹80,000 to ₹1,20,000, alongside free housing and medical care.

faqs.question: I'm 19 and in final year of graduation. NDA or CDS?
faqs.answer:
If you're below 19.5 years, you're still eligible for NDA. However, NDA means leaving college and starting 3-year training (you'll get a degree at NDA).

CDS allows you to complete your graduation first and then join for shorter training (1.5 years). If you value your current degree program, wait for CDS after graduation.

If you want the full NDA experience (most prestigious entry), apply immediately.

faqs.question: What is the pass rate for NDA?
faqs.answer:
Approximately 6-8% of written exam applicants make it to SSB. Of those who appear for SSB, about 15-20% get recommended.

Overall selection rate is roughly 1-2% of total applicants (200K+ apply, ~300-400 selected). It's competitive but achievable with focused preparation.

faqs.question: What subjects are needed for NDA?
faqs.answer:
For Army wing: Any stream (Arts/Science/Commerce) in 12th. For Navy and Air Force: Must have Physics and Mathematics in 12th.

If you want to keep all three options open, take Science with Physics + Math in 11th-12th. The written exam has Mathematics paper (Class 12 level) regardless of which wing you apply for.

faqs.question: How to prepare for NDA written exam?
faqs.answer:
Mathematics (300 marks): Class 11-12 level - focus on algebra, trigonometry, calculus, vectors, and probability. Practice NCERT + Pathfinder NDA by Arihant.

GAT (600 marks): English (200) + GK (400). English: grammar, vocabulary, comprehension.

GK: physics, chemistry, history, geography, current affairs. Read NCERT Class 9-12 for science and social studies.

faqs.question: What is the full form of NDA?
faqs.answer: NDA stands for National Defence Academy. The exam is officially the National Defence Academy and Naval Academy (NDA & NA) Examination, conducted by UPSC for officer entry into the Army, Navy and Air Force after Class 12.

faqs.question: How many times a year is the NDA exam held?
faqs.answer: UPSC conducts the NDA exam twice a year, known as NDA I (notified around December, exam in April) and NDA II (notified around May, exam in September). Each cycle has its own application window and around 400 vacancies.

NDA I 2026 ran earlier in the year. UPSC holds the NDA exam twice a year, so a fresh cycle is never far away.
